cards.text: The writer of Hebrews has spent the letter so far showing who Jesus is and what He has done (Hebrews 1:1-10:18). Now he turns to the people he calls brothers and starts with the word therefore. Friend, in a letter, therefore is the oven timer going off: something is READY.

cards.question: The writer says believers now have confidence to enter a holy place. Which one?
How do believers get that confidence to enter the Most Holy Place?
The writer calls it a new and living way, opened for us through a curtain. True or false: he says that curtain is the body of Jesus.

cards.text: A way that's already OPENED, and I spent years in a junk drawer waiting on somebody to pull the handle! The writer adds one more thing: someone is over the house of God.

cards.question: The writer adds that believers have a great ___ over the house of God.
The way in is open, and the great priest is over the house of God. So what does the writer tell them to do?

cards.text: And he says how to come: with a sincere heart, in full assurance of faith. Not hovering in the doorway like a guy who isn't sure he's at the right party.

cards.question: The writer says their hearts have been sprinkled clean. Clean of what?
True or false: the writer also says their bodies have been washed with pure water.

cards.text: Next, he tells them to hold on to the hope they profess. Not loosely, either. RESOLUTELY.

cards.question: Why can they hold on to the hope they profess so tightly?

answers.text: Their leaders keep watch over them

cards.text: Then the writer turns their eyes from themselves to each other and tells them to think about how to spur one another on. And a spur isn't a polite little tap on the shoulder, friend, it's the group chat texting, "You said gym today. I can SEE your location."

cards.question: The writer wants them to spur one another on. Toward what?
The writer warns about something some people had made a habit of. What was it?
True or false: the writer says to encourage one another less as they see the Day approaching.

cards.text: Now the writer's tone changes, and he talks about what happens if we deliberately go on sinning after we have received the knowledge of the truth. Friend, this is the part where you set the cookie down and sit up straight.

cards.question: If we deliberately keep on sinning after knowing the truth, what does the writer say no longer remains?
True or false: the writer says that then, only a fearful expectation of judgment is left.

cards.text: Judgment, and raging fire that will consume all adversaries. Then he looks back to the law of Moses, and to anyone who rejected it.

cards.question: What happened to someone who rejected the law of Moses, on the testimony of two or three witnesses?

cards.text: Then comes a hard question. If that was so under Moses, how much more severely does someone deserve to be punished who has trampled on the Son of God?

cards.question: The writer says that same person has profaned the ___ of the covenant and insulted the ___ of grace.

cards.text: The writer says we know Him who said, “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay,” and again, “The Lord will judge His people.”

cards.question: So what does the writer call falling into the hands of the living God?

cards.text: Then the writer changes gears and tells them to remember their early days in the light. Friend, it's like scrolling back to photos of your first apartment: mattress on the floor, one folding chair, and somehow you made it THROUGH.

cards.question: What did they endure back in those early days in the light?

answers.text: A great conflict in the face of suffering
A long famine across the whole land
A hard march through the desert

cards.question: True or false: sometimes they were publicly exposed to ridicule and persecution, and other times they were partners with people treated that way.

cards.text: They sympathized with those in prison, and their own property was confiscated.

cards.question: How did they accept the confiscation of their property?
Why could they take losing their property with joy?

answers.text: They had a better and permanent possession
They expected to get it all back soon
They never cared much about their things

cards.text: They lost their stuff JOYFULLY, and I lost one spot on a kitchen counter and moped in a drawer like it was my JOB. So the writer says, don't throw away your confidence.

cards.question: Why hold on to that confidence? What does the writer say it holds?
The writer tells them they need to ___, so that after they have done the will of God, they will receive what He has promised.

cards.text: Then the writer quotes Scripture (Habakkuk 2:3-4), with God speaking: “In just a little while, He who is coming will come and will not delay.

cards.question: In that same quote, God says His righteous one will live by what?
True or false: God says He takes pleasure in the one who shrinks back.
So which group does the writer say he and his readers belong to?

answers.text: Those who have faith and preserve their souls
Those who shrink back and are destroyed
Those still deciding which way to go

findings.problem: The question says believers can enter 'a holy place' and asks 'Which one?'. The right answer, 'The Most Holy Place', is the only one that repeats the question's own words. The Garden of Eden and the top of Mount Sinai don't, so the wording points to the right answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The card cites only Hebrews 10:21. Its opening line ('A way that's already OPENED') retells the way opened through the curtain from Hebrews 10:20, so the citation should be Hebrews 10:20-21.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This is the first time Moses appears in the narration, but the card doesn't say who he is. It just says 'the law of Moses'.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question begins 'The writer says that same person has profaned…'. 'That same person' refers back to the one who tramples on the Son of God in story card 6, which is no longer on screen. The question should say who is meant.

rule.text: **Always give context in the question.** The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Blank 2 ('insulted the ___ of grace') asks the baker to guess the exact wording 'Spirit of grace'. Nothing earlier in the walkthrough mentions the Spirit, so the baker can't reason it out. The distractors 'law' and 'name' fit the phrase just as well. Blank 1 ('blood' of the covenant) can be reasoned from 10:19, but blank 2 is a wording guess.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card says the writer 'quotes Scripture (Habakkuk 2:3-4), with God speaking'. Hebrews 10:37-38 doesn't match the BSB wording of Habakkuk 2:3-4. Habakkuk 2:3 says the vision 'will surely come', not 'He who is coming will come', and 'if he shrinks back' isn't in BSB Habakkuk 2:4. The opening words 'In just a little while' echo Isaiah 26:20. The card presents Habakkuk 2:3-4 as the source of wording that the BSB Habakkuk text doesn't contain.
findings.question: When a New Testament passage quotes the Old Testament in wording that differs from the BSB of the source verse (for example, following the Greek Old Testament), should Papa Dorin name the source reference, name it with a softer word like 'echoing', or leave it out? And should combined sources like Isaiah 26:20 with Habakkuk 2:3-4 be listed together?
